entries.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of advanced concepts, theories and principles in Biology
entries.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an advanced understanding of concepts, theories and principles in Biology
entries.learning_activity: (a) Describe the concept of the cell (cell theory, organelles and biological molecules)
teaching_learning_activities: Brainstorming: Guide students to brainstorm on the concept of the cell theory
Group discussions: Guide the students to discuss structures of typical cells and biological molecules of cell
ICT-based learning: Guide students to explore structure and functions of cells through animations
Laboratory Practical: Guide students to use prepared microscope slides to explore typical cells and their structures
Laboratory Practical: organise and guide students to conduct biochemical tests on the organic components of the cell
entries.assessment: The concept of the cell is correctly described
entries.references: TIE, Biology for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.learning_activity: (e) Explain the concept of gaseous exchange in plants (mechanism and theories of stomata opening and closing)
teaching_learning_activities: Brainstorming: Guide students to brainstorm the concept of gaseous exchange in plants through think-ink-share to brainstorm
Group discussion: In manageable groups, guide students to discuss the mechanism and theories governing opening and closing of stomata
ICT-based learning: Guide students to explore the mechanism of gaseous exchange in plants using animations or video
Laboratory practical: Guide students to observe and measure different factors affecting opening and closing of stomata
Case Study: Guide students to analyse the adaptation plants in a drought-stricken area that allow the plant to conserve water while still allowing gaseous exchange
entries.assessment: Concept of gaseous exchange in plants is clearly explained
resources: diagrams and videos on plant adaptations
entries.references: TIE, Biology for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.learning_activity: (d) Describe the distinctive characteristics of kingdoms, phyla/ divisions and class (Monera, Protoctista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia)
teaching_learning_activities: Jigsaw: Guide students through jigsaw to explore features of each comparative group of classification
Laboratory practicals: Guide students to carry out dissection of the selected animal to explore different systems
Snow-balling: summarise the economic importance of living organisms through snow-balling
Project activity: Guide students to perform activities such as growing different products, such as mushrooms, fruit trees
Exploration: Guide students to explore features of the dissected mammals using digital simulations.
entries.assessment: Distinctive characteristics of kingdoms, phyla/ divisions and class are correctly described
resources: Varieties of living organisms (preserved or fresh) examples: yeast, bread mould, mushroom, Tilapia fish, crabs, moss plant, fern plant, conifers, mouse/rat, frog/toad, flowering plants, hand lens, dissecting kit, dissecting dish, pins,
chloroform, diagrams, charts videos and models showing dissected animals
entries.references: TIE, Biology for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

teaching_learning_activities: Exploration: Guide the students through animations or videos to explore steps for carrying out anatomical and physiological investigations related to digestive and excretory systems, photosynthesis, and gaseous exchange in living organisms

Laboratory practicals: Organise and guide students to carry out anatomical and physiological investigations related to digestive and excretory systems, photosynthesis, and gaseous exchange in living organisms
entries.assessment: Anatomical and physiological investigations are correctly designed and carried out
entries.references: TIE, Biology for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education
